meta.title: Africa's Borders Were Drawn With a Ruler
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note: This script highlights several real sovereign countries at once (all real polygons in country-codes.json: EG, LY, TD, NE, NA, BW) instead of one single target, because their shared straight-line edges are the whole visual point. No custom lines/markers stand in for a missing polygon here -- every highlighted country is real.

beats.voText: Look closely at a map of Africa and you'll see it, dozens of perfectly straight lines slicing across the entire continent.
Most were decided at the 1884 Berlin Conference, by European powers who had barely set foot on the land they were dividing.
Those straight lines cut through rivers, mountain ranges, and ethnic groups that had nothing to do with drawing them.
Nearly half of Africa's modern borders are still perfectly straight lines today, more than anywhere else on Earth.
beats.onScreenText: Nearly half are still straight lines.

beats.voText: One border between Namibia and Botswana runs so precisely straight that it was fixed with a single line of longitude on a map.
beats.onScreenText: One line of longitude. A border.

beats.voText: A continent's borders, ruled straight by people who'd never walked the land, the ruler marks of a meeting none of them attended. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
